annotations.annotation_text: Viconian marker "Thunder" on page 175 ("Shem the Penman"): Giambattista Vico's cyclical philosophy — divine, heroic, and human ages followed by thundering ricorso — structures this passage within Joyce's devastating self-portrait as Shem the forger-artist who writes on his own skin with bodily secretions. The current Age of Gods phase shapes the language, institutional imagery, and historical echoes of the dream.
sources: Beckett, Samuel. Dante... Bruno. Vico.. Joyce. https://archive.org/details/ourexagminationr0000unse
Ricorso.net: Viconian Structure in FW. https://www.ricorso.net

annotations.annotation_text: Fall/resurrection motif "Broken" on page 175 ("Shem the Penman"): Tim Finnegan tumbling from his ladder, Humpty Dumpty shattering from the wall, Adam falling in Eden — all converge within Joyce's devastating self-portrait as Shem the forger-artist who writes on his own skin with bodily secretions. The comic-cosmic Fall during the Age of Gods phase demands its counterpart: resurrection through the whiskey-splash of the water of life (uisce beatha).
sources: The Ballad of Tim Finnegan's Wake. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finnegan%27s_Wake
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
Opie, Iona and Peter. The Oxford Dictionary of Nursery Rhymes. https://archive.org/details/oxforddictionary0000unse_m4u1
